title: Existence and uniqueness of the characteristic polynomial on a finite locally free module of constant rank
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ an integer, $M$ an $A$-module and $\varphi:M\to M$ an $A$-linear map. Assume there are $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that for each $i$ the $A_{f_i}$-module $M_{f_i}$ is free of rank $n$. Then there is exactly one polynomial $\chi\in A[T]$ with the following property: for every ring map $A\to A'$ such that $M\otimes_AA'$ is a free $A'$-module of rank $n$, the image of $\chi$ in $A'[T]$ is the characteristic polynomial $\det(T\cdot1-\varphi_{A'})$ of $\varphi_{A'}=\varphi\otimes1$ on $M\otimes_AA'$ (computed in any basis). Moreover $\chi=T^n+c_{n-1}T^{n-1}+\dots+c_0$ with $c_k\in A$ (in particular $\chi$ is monic). In particular, if $M$ itself is free of rank $n$, then $\chi$ is the usual characteristic polynomial of $\varphi$.

proof.text: *Local polynomials.* For each $i$ let $\varphi_{f_i}:M_{f_i}\to M_{f_i}$, $m/f_i^e\mapsto\varphi(m)/f_i^e$; it is well defined and $A_{f_i}$-linear, being the map corresponding to $\varphi\otimes1$ under $M\otimes_AA_{f_i}\cong M_{f_i}$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor]. As $M_{f_i}$ is free of rank $n$ over $A_{f_i}$, let $\chi_i\in A_{f_i}[T]$ be the characteristic polynomial of $\varphi_{f_i}$ in a basis of $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module]; it does not depend on the basis and $\chi_i=T^n+(\text{terms of degree}<n)$ [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties (a), (c)].

Details omitted.'

proof.text: *Local comparison.* Fix $i$ and a ring map $A\to B$ under which $f_i$ maps to a unit. By the universal property of $A\to A_{f_i}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] there is exactly one ring map $A_{f_i}\to B$ compatible with the maps from $A$. Then there are isomorphisms of $B$-modules $M\otimes_AB\cong(M\otimes_AA_{f_i})\otimes_{A_{f_i}}B$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-transitive, with $A\to A_{f_i}\to B$] and $(M\otimes_AA_{f_i})\otimes_{A_{f_i}}B\cong M_{f_i}\otimes_{A_{f_i}}B$ (base change along $A_{f_i}\to B$ [def-weil-module-base-change] of the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor]); by the naturality clauses of both lemmas the composite carries $\varphi\otimes1_B$ to $(\varphi\otimes1_{A_{f_i}})\otimes1_B$ and then to $\varphi_{f_i}\otimes1_B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] (d), $M_{f_i}\otimes_{A_{f_i}}B$ is free of rank $n$ over $B$ and the characteristic polynomial of $\varphi_{f_i}\otimes1_B$ is the image of $\chi_i$ under $A_{f_i}[T]\to B[T]$; by (b) of the same lemma, transported along the isomorphism: *$M\otimes_AB$ is free of rank $n$ over $B$ and $\det(T-\varphi\otimes1_B)$ is the image of $\chi_i$ in $B[T]$.*

proof.text: *Agreement on overlaps.* Fix $i,j$ and take $B=A_{f_if_j}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], in which $f_i$ and $f_j$ are units (they divide the unit $f_if_j$). The ring map $A_{f_i}\to A_{f_if_j}$ of the previous step is the canonical map $x/f_i^e\mapsto f_j^ex/(f_if_j)^e$ (it is compatible with the maps from $A$, and such a map is unique), and likewise for $j$. Applying the previous step once with $i$ and once with $j$: the images of $\chi_i$ and of $\chi_j$ in $A_{f_if_j}[T]$ are both equal to $\det(T-\varphi\otimes1)$ on $M\otimes_AA_{f_if_j}$, hence equal. Since a ring map acts on polynomials coefficientwise, for every $k\ge0$ the $T^k$-coefficients $c_{i,k}\in A_{f_i}$ of $\chi_i$ and $c_{j,k}\in A_{f_j}$ of $\chi_j$ have the same image in $A_{f_if_j}$.

Details omitted.'

proof.text: *Gluing.* For each $k\ge0$ the family $(c_{i,k})_i$ agrees on overlaps (previous step), so by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue] (ii) there is exactly one $c_k\in A$ with $c_k/1=c_{i,k}$ in $A_{f_i}$ for all $i$. For $k>n$ all $c_{i,k}=0$ and for $k=n$ all $c_{i,n}=1$ (first step), so by the uniqueness in (ii) $c_k=0$ for $k>n$ and $c_n=1$. Put $\chi=\sum_{k=0}^nc_kT^k=T^n+c_{n-1}T^{n-1}+\dots+c_0\in A[T]$ (in particular monic of degree $n$). By construction the image of $\chi$ in $A_{f_i}[T]$ is $\chi_i$ for every $i$.

proof.text: *$\chi$ has the property.* Let $\rho:A\to A'$ be a ring map with $N=M\otimes_AA'$ free of rank $n$ over $A'$; put $\psi=\varphi\otimes1$ and $P=\det(T-\psi)\in A'[T]$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module], which does not depend on the basis [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] (a). Write $1=\sum_ia_if_i$; then $1=\sum_i\rho(a_i)g_i$ with $g_i=\rho(f_i)$, so $g_1,\dots,g_r$ generate the unit ideal of $A'$. Fix $i$ and let $B_i=A'_{g_i}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], an $A$-algebra via $A\to A'\to B_i$ in which $f_i$ maps to the unit $g_i$. (1) By the local comparison step, $\det(T-\varphi\otimes1_{B_i}\mid M\otimes_AB_i)$ is the image of $\chi_i$ under $A_{f_i}[T]\to B_i[T]$; as $A\to A_{f_i}\to B_i$ equals $A\to A'\to B_i$ and $\chi\mapsto\chi_i$ (gluing step), this is the image of $\rho(\chi)\in A'[T]$ in $B_i[T]$. (2) $N\otimes_{A'}B_i\cong M\otimes_AB_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-transitive, with $A\to A'\to B_i$], carrying $\psi\otimes1_{B_i}$ to $\varphi\otimes1_{B_i}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] (d) the characteristic polynomial of $\psi\otimes1_{B_i}$ is the image of $P$ in $B_i[T]$, and by (b) it equals $\det(T-\varphi\otimes1_{B_i})$. So $\rho(\chi)$ and $P$ have the same image in $A'_{g_i}[T]$ for every $i$; applying [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue] (i) over $A'$ with $g_1,\dots,g_r$ to each coefficient of $\rho(\chi)-P$ gives $\rho(\chi)=P$.

proof.text: *Uniqueness.* Let $\tilde\chi\in A[T]$ have the property of the statement. For each $i$, the local comparison step with $B=A_{f_i}$ shows that $M\otimes_AA_{f_i}$ is free of rank $n$ and $\det(T-\varphi\otimes1)=\chi_i$ on it; so the property applied to $A\to A_{f_i}$ gives: the image of $\tilde\chi$ in $A_{f_i}[T]$ is $\chi_i$, which is the image of $\chi$ (gluing step). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue] (i) to each coefficient of $\tilde\chi-\chi$ gives $\tilde\chi=\chi$.

proof.text: *The free case.* If $M$ is free of rank $n$, take $A'=A$ ($\rho=\mathrm{id}$): the map $M\otimes_AA\to M$, $m\otimes a\mapsto am$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-module-base-change] carrying $\varphi\otimes1$ to $\varphi$, so $M\otimes_AA$ is free of rank $n$ and, by the property and [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] (b), $\chi=\det(T-\varphi\otimes1)=\det(T-\varphi\mid M)$, the characteristic polynomial of $\varphi$ in any basis of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module].
